pf.quest.chapter.welcome.desc:
While working on our new Quantum Technology Thingy (tm pending), we made a tiny mistake which led to you being teleported to this new world.

Oops... anyways...

We're not sure what dangers or hardships await you on this journey, but at least you were teleported with our survival kit, which grants you basic shelter and some starting resources.

We hope you'll find a way to use your knowledge and that weird alchemy hobby of yours to hopefully get back to us, while we try to repair the Quantum Technology Thingy (tm pending).
pf.quest.chapter.welcome.thanks.title: Thanks

Gac
pf.quest.chapter.welcome.bug.title: Found a bug?
pf.quest.chapter.welcome.bug.desc:
If you found a bug, something wrong with the modpack, or just have feedback, then feel free to reach out to me:

https://github.com/gigili
https://x.com/Gac_BL
pf.quest.chapter.welcome.starting_resour:
The survival kit includes some of the basic resources you'll need to get started on this journey.

Inside the base, there's a basic kitchen setup for you, so you can make yourself some food.

It also includes your alchemy table, which we still don't quite understand how it'll help you, but you do you, I guess...

We've also included some useful tools and resources to help you out as well.

Good luck \& have fun!
pf.quest.chapter.welcome.multiplayer.des:
- For multiplayer it is recommended to remove the schematics from the config/startstrucutes folder and only add a schematic to config/pf_schematics. 

- There is a config file: config/projectflattenedutilities-common.toml
  Inside of  which you can whitelist which players are allowed to use spawnHouse command

- /spawnHouse <fileName>
  Spawns a structure at the player's current location.
  <fileName> is optional; defaults to default_base if not specified.
  All .nbt files should be placed in: /config/pf_schematics 
  This command can only be run once per player (unless reset with /clearHouse).

- /clearHouse [playerName]
  Resets a player's ability to use /spawnHouse.
  Requires permission level 2 or higher. 
  [playerName] is optional. If not provided, it applies to the executing player.

- Check out Project Flattened Utilities mod for more info
pf.quest.chapter.welcome.security.title: Security
pf.quest.chapter.welcome.security.desc:
Since we never know what kind of environment our exploration teams might encounter, we've included some basic protection for you.

In one of the barrels, you will find some sentries that should help keep your base safe from possible intruders.

There is also a small perimeter just outside your base that you can use to place your turrets and cameras on.

&4&lNOTE:&r &4Sentries can sometimes disappear from your world if they are not inside a loaded chunk.&r

So keep your base loaded and safe.
pf.quest.chapter.qol.desc: These are just some of the mods available to improve your experience
pf.quest.chapter.qol.gadgets.laser_io.de: No more DireWire when you have lasers
pf.quest.chapter.qol.gadgets.constructio: Why place every block manually when you can use a magic wand to help you
pf.quest.chapter.qol.gadgets.modular_rou: A nice way to automate things with
pf.quest.chapter.qol.gadgets.iron_furnac: Tired of waiting for things to smelt?\n\nNow you don't have to, just upgrade your regular furnace for faster smelting.
pf.quest.chapter.qol.gadgets.builder.des: You can build or mine large areas with this machine
pf.quest.chapter.qol.gadgets.jetpack.des: Would you rather walk 1000 blocks or fly there super fast?
pf.quest.chapter.qol.security.universal_: You will need this wrench in order to be able to pick up blocks from this mod.
pf.quest.chapter.qol.security.camera_mon: You can use this item to look at your connected cameras
pf.quest.chapter.qol.security.ubr.desc: With this you can make almost any block blast proof and unmineable
pf.quest.chapter.qol.security.camera.des: Monitor your surroundings without leaving your base or maybe from a secure bunker?
pf.quest.chapter.qol.security.sentry.des:
*Pew* *Pew*

Keeps the enemy away from your base.

It has multiple modes which can be toggled by right clicking it.
Check your starting resources to find a sapling, or go out and explore until you find a village.

The most basic resources in this game are cobblestone, dirt, and wood.

But in a super flat world, resources are hard to come by since the world is made up of only 3 layers.

The 1st and 2nd layers are dirt

The 3rd layer is grass.

So, using some 'magic,' we've made it so the classic cobblestone generator produces more than just cobblestone.

Hint: Check out the usages for a diamond block in JEI to see more.

Most basic resources such as &6Iron&r, &cRedstone&r, &eGold&r, &3Zinc&r, &7Andesite&r can be obtained via vanilla cobble generator.\n\nCreate a vanilla cobble generator and it will produce different types of blocks to help you get started.

The way to obtain most resources in this pack is by using the sifter and a mesh.

Each mesh has different outputs and requirements.

It is recommended to check out each mesh by pressing U while hovering over it in JEI.

Advanced meshes require a brass sifter to work.

For some items, it is also required that the sifter be waterlogged.

{@pagebreak}To use a sifter you can either drop items on top of it so it can pick them up, or you can use a hopper to insert them into it (pipes and chutes work as well).

When pulling items out of the sifter, you can right click on it to get the items inside or use a hopper (can be slow at extracting) or something like a chute or item pipe.

With mechanical drills, you can easily automate the breaking of ores from the custom cobblestone generator.

This allows you to focus on other tasks while ores are mined in the background.

With a bit of help from some fans and either water or lava, you can even automate the processing as well.

Mechanical drills can also be enchanted to yield more resources as they mine.

Lava is dangerous—but also renewable with the right setup!

Place a source block of lava on top of a solid block, then hang a pointed dripstone underneath it.

Below that, place a cauldron.

Over time, the lava will begin to drip through the dripstone, and the cauldron will slowly fill with lava.

Once full, you can scoop it up with a bucket—effectively turning one lava source into many.

It's slow, but it's infinite and fully automatable!

&lVisual tip:&r

Check the image on the right for how to set it up properly.
Nobody wants to mine cobble forever, so it's best to automate it.\n\nYou might want to consider duplicating your lava first before setting this up, as you won't get it back.

As this modpack focuses on EMC, I can't make it too easy and let you keep upgrading this further.\n\nTier 2 is as far as it goes, but it should help you get up and running quickly until you can automate EMC and get EMC links.
Sand can be obtained by using a Create mill or Crushing Wheels to crush gravel into sand.
Dust can be obtained by using a Create mill or Crushing Wheels to crush sand into dust.
pf.quest.chapter.getting_started.getting: It can be used to grind down certain items.\n\nFor example, you could grind down coal into black dye or gravel into sand.

You can use pipes, hoppers or chutes to insert and pull items out of the sifter.

Do note that hoppers are the slowest option and will create a backlog of items in sifters because of their slow speed.

Pipes with upgrades or chutes are a better option.
String, Andesite and Zinc meshes are a good starting point for getting more resources.
With a brass mesh, you can start getting crushed raw ores.\n\nWhich can then be washed to get even more resources.
With an advanced brass mesh, you get even better chances for your sifters to produce resources, and you can also get some rare materials as well.
Once you have obtained the basin, you can start mixing certain things to produce new ones.\n\nOne example of this is combining copper and zinc to produce brass.

When mixing items or fluids together, sometimes they have a special heat requirement in order for them to mix.

In order to heat up the basin, you can use the blaze burner under it.

To fuel the blaze burner and produce normal heat you can use any burnable item such as: coal, charcoal.

If you wish to use a lava bucket or fill blaze burners with lava, you will need to give them a straw first.

To fill a blaze burner, you need to right click an empty blaze burner on the Blaze or a blaze spawner.

To fill your blaze burner you would need to go to the Nether first and find a blaze there.

Then you would right click on that blaze with your empty blaze burner to capture it.

With this egg, you can spawn the blaze without having to go to the Nether and look for one.

But sometimes exploration can be faster than automation or maybe more fun depending on your play style.

Now that you have acquired brass, it is time to upgrade your sifters and meshes to a new tier.

With brass tier unlocked, you can get more resources with better chances than before.

It also allows you to craft more advanced Create components such as: Precision Mechanism, Electric Motors, Mechanical Arms and many more.

Crushing wheels can speed up the processing of resources.

They can be used to turn gravel into sand and sand into dust, which can then be sifted for additional resources.

They can also crush End Stone into Crushed End Stone.

This is especially useful during the early game when you don't have EMC links or much EMC to constantly extract gravel and/or sand for sifting.

End stone can be obtained by going to the end and mining the end island or it can be crafted.\n\nTo reach the end you need to find the stronghold in the world, just like you do in vanilla game using Eyes of Ender.
pf.quest.chapter.getting_started.ore_pro: Soul Sand can be obtained by either going to the neter or by crafting it using a Create Mixer.

The Encased Fan is a versatile machine powered by rotational force.

By placing it facing different directions and combining it with elements like lava, water, or fire, you can unlock unique processing effects:

&cLava&r in front = smelting items

&9Water&r in front = washing items

&6Fire&r in front = haunting items (with Soul Fire) or cooking (with Camp Fire)

Empty space = pushing entities or items

It's a key part of many Create automation setups and lets you build fully modular processing stations.

The Fan Catalyst is a versatile utility block designed for use with the Encased Fan.\n\nIt can safely contain and simulate the effects of various catalysts like lava, water, campfire, or soul fire, enabling clean and compact automation setups without needing the actual fluid or fire sources.

The Squeezer is a powerful tool for ore processing.

By placing raw ores inside, it compresses and crushes them with a chance to double the output—giving you more resources from the same input.

It doesn't guarantee double every time, but with enough tries, you'll see a significant increase in yield.

Perfect for early automation or getting the most out of rare ores!

The Mechanical Squeezer takes the manual work out of ore processing.

Unlike its manual counterpart, this fully automated machine can be powered with energy and run continuously, squeezing ores, plants, and other materials with increased efficiency and automation support.

It often provides better chances for double outputs, and can also handle more advanced recipes like producing fluids or organic materials—depending on the mods installed.

Say goodbye to hand-cranking and hello to industrial power!

Tired of waiting for one item at a time to finish smelting before you can start the next?

This upgrade changes everything.

With it installed, your furnace or smelter gains the ability to process multiple stacks simultaneously or split a stack into parallel operations, drastically improving throughput.

Even better—no more coal or burnable fuels required. Instead, the upgrade converts your smelter into a power-driven machine, requiring a steady supply of FE (Forge Energy) or equivalent modded power.

Ever feel like waiting for items to smelt is a drag? You're not alone.

That's where Speed Upgrades come in!

By installing this upgrade into your furnace or smelter, you'll significantly reduce the time it takes to process items.

The higher the furnace tier, the more noticeable the effect—but be warned: faster smelting also means higher power consumption.

It's all about balance—more speed, more power, more output!

What if your furnace could do more than just smelt?

With this upgrade installed, your furnace loses its ability to smelt items, but gains a new function: burning fuel to generate power.

Feed it burnable items like coal, charcoal, or wood, and it will convert them into usable energy for your machines.

Perfect for early-game setups or as a backup power source when your main generator runs dry.

Tired of constantly feeding fuel into your furnace?

The Fuel Efficiency Augment is here to help.

When installed into any compatible Iron Furnace, this upgrade reduces the amount of fuel consumed per item smelted, making your resources go much further.

The higher the furnace tier, the greater the fuel savings—perfect for stretching your coal, charcoal, or other burnables over longer sessions.
Provide the transmitter block with power (energy) and then use the receiving item to connect them.\n\nOnce connected, you can put the receiver into the furnace instead of coal.
pf.quest.chapter.getting_started.mob_far:
If you want to create spawn eggs to customize the spawners, you can use a swab on a mob.

Then combine it with some liquid XP and a seed to get a Chick Feed.

Feed it to a chicken, and it should generate a spawn egg of the swabbed mob.
Feed a chicken with the GM Chicken Feed Cursed to get a Rotten Egg.
Feed a chicken with a Nutritious Chicken Feed to get a Golden Egg.

Spawns hostile mobs and requires darkness to work.

If exposed to sunlight, it will burn and destroy the cursed earth.

It can be picked up with Silk Touch.

Spawns passive mobs and needs constant light to work; otherwise, it gets covered in snow.

It can be picked up with Silk Touch.

It will periodically spawn grass over it, so you'll need to remove it before it resumes mob spawning.
Good for storing large amounts of XP.
This will allow you to store an almost limitless supply of experience from your mob farm.\n\nBut it needs to be either piped in from the top or use an XP tap to pour your experience into it.

The Deep Mob Learner is the heart of Hostile Neural Networks.

It allows you to “teach” a neural network how to fight mobs by feeding it data from their defeats.

To begin, you'll need to craft a Deep Mob Learner and a Data Model.

Right click with an empty Model Framework on a mob you would like to sample.

Insert the Model Framework into the learner and start collecting “mob data” by killing that specific mob while holding the learner.

As you gain data, the model levels up, improving the loot you'll receive from simulation and real combat.

Once you're ready, use the Simulation Chamber to farm resources virtually—no need to risk your life!

Before your Deep Mob Learner can begin its training, it needs a Model Framework—the foundation for any learning process.

This item is a blank slate ready to be imprinted with knowledge of a specific mob.

Crafting a Model Framework is the first step toward automated mob drops and powerful resource generation.

Once crafted, right click the desired mob to tune your Model Framework to that specific mob.

Place the tuned Model Framework into the Deep Learner and start killing that mob.

The more mobs of that type you kill, the more advanced the Model Framework model becomes, having a higher chance to produce a prediction.

To simulate mobs and generate their valuable drops without ever swinging a sword, you'll need a Prediction Matrix.

This is the fuel that powers the Simulation Chamber, allowing it to run virtual encounters using your trained Model Frameworks.

You'll go through these quickly during large-scale automation, so set up a crafting or automation system to keep them flowing.

The Simulation Chamber is where the magic of Hostile Neural Networks truly begins.

By combining a trained Model Framework with Prediction Matrices, you can simulate mob encounters—no danger involved!

While working, the machine can produce either a mob prediction or a generalized prediction.

Mob prediction means that the simulation of a kill of that mob was a success and a generalized one means it failed.

Higher tiers of Model Frameworks have fewer chances to produce generalized predictions.

The Loot Fabricator turns pristine matter into real, usable mob drops of your choosing.

No need for messy mob farms—this machine lets you pick what you want and get it instantly.

As long as you provide some power and mob predictions.

It's especially useful for rare drops or hostile mobs that are difficult to farm normally.
pf.quest.chapter.enchanting.hyper_enchan: You can send nuggets of experience or any enchanted item into the disenchanter to pull the XP into the tank.\n\nOr, you can stand on it and let it drain your XP.

Printer can be used to duplicate enchanted books.

Regular enchants require liquid experience.

Higher level enchants require hyper experience.

Regular books require ink.

Right-click in the air to open its GUI.

Place an enchanted book to select which enchantment you want to apply.

Right-click the blaze burner with it and provide the liquid experience or hyper experience based on the enchantment level.

If you are using hyper experience then you will get +1 on the level of enchantment that you're trying to apply.

Hyper Experience is used for hyper or over-enchanting.\n\nIn vanilla Minecraft, the highest level of the Looting enchantment is 3 — but with hyper enchanting, you can push it beyond that, reaching up to level 4.
pf.quest.chapter.enchanting.apotheosis.i:
Infusion is a special version of Enchanting used for better enchantments.

When the right amount of &aEterna&r, &cQuanta&r, and &5Arcana&r is reached the enchantments will offer Infusion.

(To know the levels needed you can check JEI).
pf.quest.chapter.enchanting.apotheosis.h: Can be obtained by fishing for it.
pf.quest.chapter.enchanting.apotheosis.e:
Tired of enchanted books cluttering your chests or storage systems?

Maybe it's time to return them to the library.

The Library block lets you store all your enchanted books and later retrieve any enchantment you need.

The highest enchantment level you can retrieve is based on the books you've stored.

For example, if you store 1 Looting Level 3 book and 3 Looting Level 1 books, you'll be able to retrieve up to 2 Looting Level 3 books.
pf.quest.chapter.enchanting.apotheosis.l:
A grand upgrade to the humble Enchanting Library, the Library of Alexandria offers vastly expanded storage for your enchanted books.

No more overflowing chests or cluttered shelves — this arcane archive lets you store a massive collection of enchantments in one place and retrieve them as needed.

The highest level of any enchantment you can withdraw depends on what you've already stored. The more powerful books you contribute, the more powerful your retrievals can be.

Build it, fill it, and never worry about running out of your favorite enchantments again.
pf.quest.chapter.projecte.emc.philosophe:
A mysterious relic, brimming with power.

The Philosopher's Stone is your gateway to alchemical mastery.

It can transmute basic materials, convert fuels, and is essential for crafting higher-tier alchemical devices.

Experiment with it in your inventory, on a crafting table, or even in-world. You'll be surprised at how many recipes it can unlock.
pf.quest.chapter.projecte.emc.transmutat:
The Transmutation Table is the core of ProjectE's alchemy system.

It lets you store and convert items based on their EMC value — an energy-based currency of matter.

Feed it items to learn their EMC, then exchange any learned item for another, as long as you have enough EMC.

No more overflowing chests — your resources are now pure energy.

Tip: Pair this with energy/fuel generation for unlimited item access.

The Portable Transmutation Tablet brings the power of the Transmutation Table to your hands — anytime, anywhere.

No need to run back to your base; open your tablet and transmute on the go.

Perfect for adventuring, building, or managing resources while off exploring.

Unlocks: Total freedom in resource management.
pf.quest.chapter.projecte.emc.infinite_s:
No more searching for food!

Exchange some of your EMC for a free meal.

cWARNING: When crafting this, the Transmutation Tablet will be consumed.r
pf.quest.chapter.projecte.emc.infinite_c:
No more searching for coal!

Use this item instead to get infinite fuel for your furnace.

cWARNING: Crafting this item will consume the Transmutation Tablet. r
pf.quest.chapter.projecte.emc.transmutat: With this block, you will be able to access all of your items from the transmutation table inside your AE2 system.\n\nIt pairs perfectly with auto-crafting of items, as you don't have to pull them out of your transmutation table or tablet first.
Power Flowers are the ultimate passive EMC generators in ProjectE.

Once placed, they require no input, no fuel, and no sunlight — they simply generate EMC over time based on their tier.

Each Power Flower tier produces EMC faster than the last, with higher-tier versions generating millions of EMC per second.

Place them down, and they'll start passively filling your Transmutation Table or Energy Condenser with EMC automatically.

Build more, upgrade often, and let the EMC flow.
pf.quest.chapter.power.powah.desc:
The Reactor is a multi-block (FE) generator that uses Uraninite as main fuel.

To build it you will need 36 Reactor blocks in your hand and placing them in a 3X4 replaceable area, then the reactor will complete building itself automatically.

{@pagebreak}When generating energy, the reactor heats up causing it to consume fuel faster and generate less FE/t, so you need to cool it down using a coolant like water.

Also, you can use a solid coolant like snow or ice for extra coldness. Solid coolant requires liquid coolant to work.

Keep the reactor buffer full of fuel for better production.
pf.quest.chapter.power.powah.coal.desc: Carbon materials like coal, wood... will improve the fuel efficiency and will add +180 °C of heat.
pf.quest.chapter.power.powah.redstone.de: Redstone will speed up the production and the fuel consumption and will add +120 °C of heat.
pf.quest.chapter.power.powah.dry_ice.des: Dry Ice used mainly to cool down reactors.\n\nIt can be obtained by energizing two pieces of blue ice.
pf.quest.chapter.storage.basic_storage.c: With a compression upgrade, your Limited Barrel II, III can be used same as compacting drawers.
pf.quest.chapter.storage.basic_storage.l: For this modpack, I've decided not to include mods like Functional Storage or Storage Drawers, as Sophisticated Storage is already part of the pack.\n\nIt can do almost everything the other mods can, and even more.
pf.quest.chapter.storage.integrated_dyna:
Integrated Dynamics offers a lot to players and can sometimes be scary to play with.

But don't worry, I'll guide you on how to use this mod to set up a nice little storage system.

It will have basic crafting, as well as auto-crafting functionality.

With this, you can connect your chests and barrels to the network and access them through the terminal.\n\nThere are other interfaces available as well that allow you to import or export items, fluids, or energy to and from your network.

This is used to view all the contents of your storage network.

You can use this screen to insert items into storage, as well as take them out.

Once you have autocrafting set up, you'll also be able to request items to be crafted automatically.

This can be attached to crafting tables to automatically craft any recipe that can be made in a crafting table.\n\nYou can also attach it to other blocks, such as furnaces, to automate the smelting process.

The Logic Programmer is the heart of Integrated Dynamics automation.

With it, you can create powerful variable-based logic to control machines, networks, and even redstone—all without writing a single line of code.

Use the Logic Programmer to define variables, functions, and operators that can be stored in variable cards and placed into logic-based machines.

This tool is essential for anyone looking to go beyond simple cables and dive into smart automation.

Hint:

It might look overwhelming at first, but start small—try creating a simple Boolean or number variable to get familiar with how it works!
This is a portable version of the Logic Programmer.

As your logic network grows, you'll need a place to keep all those clever variables you've programmed. The Variable Store acts like a memory bank for your Logic Programmer creations.

Each Variable Store holds multiple variable cards and makes them accessible to nearby machines and logic components on the network.

Without it, your beautifully crafted variables might get... forgotten.

Need to connect two parts of your Integrated Dynamics network but can't run cables through walls, dimensions, or long distances? The Omni-Directional Connector has you covered.

These connectors create a wireless link between distant parts of your network, as long as they share the same channel. It's like teleportation—but for logic cables.

Perfect for keeping your base clean, compact, and connected or getting a remote access to your storage.

Ever wish you could access your entire storage network while out exploring or deep underground? The Portable Storage Terminal makes that dream a reality.

This handy device lets you wirelessly browse, insert, and extract items from your Integrated Dynamics network—no cables required.

Just link it to your network once, and you’ll have remote access wherever you go... as long as the network is loaded and chunk-loaded.

Once your autocrafting setup is ready, the Crafting Job Terminal becomes your control center for managing it all.

This terminal lets you view, monitor, and cancel active crafting jobs on your network.

It’s especially useful when things get complex—no more guessing if your items are still being made or stuck in the system!

Stay informed, stay in control.
pf.quest.chapter.storage.rftools.storage: Allows you to connect inventories in a certain range around the scanner.
pf.quest.chapter.storage.rftools.mnodula: Acts like a shulker box, allowing you to store your items in it and move it around without spilling anything when broken.
pf.quest.chapter.ae2.certus_quartz.desc:
To get started with AE2, you'll need to gather some basic resources from the mod itself.

In normal worlds, you would typically search for meteors, but since this is a flat world, meteors don't spawn.

So, you'll need to start sifting a bit to obtain the necessary resources.
pf.quest.chapter.ae2.inscriber_plate.des: Check out the inscriber recipe for each plate.\n\nOnce you have crafted them all, hold them in your inventory to complete this quest.
pf.quest.chapter.ae2.channels.desc: While in most packs when working with AE2 you need to worry about channels, in this one you don't.\n\nIt was made so that you have infinite channels available at your disposal to focus on automation instead.
pf.quest.chapter.ae2.me_disk_housing.des: If you wish to have a disk storage without type limits then AE2Things has you covered.\n\nWith AE2Things, you can make regular disks just like you would for AE2, but these disks only care about bytes and not types.
pf.quest.chapter.ae2.mega_cell.subtitle: When regular storage is not enough
pf.quest.chapter.ae2.mega_cell.desc: With Mega Cells you can store even more data on your disks than what regular disks allow.
You can also automate ore mining using an Annihilation Plane, offering a sleek and powerful alternative to mechanical drills.

When placed next to a custom cobblestone generator, the Annihilation Plane will instantly break any generated blocks, automatically collecting the drops into your storage system — no moving parts required.

Even better, the Annihilation Plane supports enchantments, allowing you to boost its efficiency. Add enchantments like Fortune to increase the number of resources gained per operation, or Silk Touch if you need specific block types.

With the right setup, this method provides a fully automated, enchantment-enhanced mining solution that runs silently and efficiently in the background.
pf.quest.chapter.ae2.extended_ae.extende:
The Extended Inscriber takes automation to the next level, allowing up to four inscribing jobs to run simultaneously!

No more bottlenecks when crafting processors or pressing materials for your ME System.

Just like the standard Inscriber, it features a button to adjust the max stack size in its inventory.

However, when using it with a Pattern Provider, it's recommended to set the stack size to 1 to prevent potential issues.

Streamline your processor production and supercharge your Applied Energistics 2 automation with the Extended Inscriber!
pf.quest.chapter.ae2.wireless_kit:
No more endless cable runs—wirelessly link your ME Networks!

The ME Wireless Connector allows you to connect networks over short distances within the same dimension.

Use the ME Wireless Setup Kit to pair two connectors and establish a link.

Keep in mind:

- Longer distances consume more energy, increasing exponentially.

- Only same-colored connectors link together—use a Color Applicator to organize connections.

- Energy Cards can help reduce power costs.
pf.quest.chapter.ae2.extended_molecular_:
The Extended Molecular Assembler is a faster, more powerful alternative to the standard Molecular Assembler, running 8 crafting jobs at the same time and operating at twice the speed!

To take full advantage of its capabilities, make sure your ME Network has enough Crafting Accelerators.

However, unlike the regular assembler, this version only accepts crafting jobs from a Pattern Provider—you cannot place patterns directly inside it.
pf.quest.chapter.ae2.extended_ae.assembl:
No more sprawling walls or messy chandeliers of Molecular Assemblers and Pattern Providers!

With the Assembler Matrix, all your autocrafting needs are handled within a single, powerful multiblock structure, capable of reaching a maximum size of 7×7×7.

The Assembler Matrix is fully modular, allowing you to configure it to suit your needs.

It requires a mix of Pattern Cores and Craft Cores to function, ensuring seamless automation of even the most complex recipes.

To maximize its speed, you can install up to 5 Speed Cores. However, adding more than 5 Speed Cores provides no additional benefit.

If you're tired of cluttered setups and inefficient crafting, the Assembler Matrix is the ultimate solution for a streamlined Applied Energistics 2 autocrafting system!
pf.quest.chapter.ae2.advanced_ae.qunatum: These blocks provide the framing of the quantum computer.\n\nThey are used as a building block for the quantum computer and connect everything together.
pf.quest.chapter.ae2.advanced_ae.quantum: Similarly to the Data Entanglers, multi-threaders enable accelerators to run extra threads in separate dimensions, multiplying their co-processing power by 4. Only one of these can be placed in each quantum computer multiblock.

These blocks expand the crafting storage of the quantum core.\n\nThey effectively increase the amount of concurrent tasks the quantum computer is able to run. There are two variations, with 128M and 256M of capacity.

The Quantum core is the heart of the Quantum Computer.

It has 256M of crafting storage and 8 co-processor threads by itself.

It's the only block that can create a formed quantum computer by itself and provide all the benefits of a quantum computer.

However, if used to create a multiblock, a much more powerful computer can be created.

When used as a standalone computer, power must be provided through the Up or Down sides, where the connectors are.

Data Entanglers are a special block that affect all storage blocks present in the multiblock.

They enable storage blocks to store data in several dimensions, effectively multiplying their storage by 4.

Only one of these can be placed in each quantum computer multiblock.

Quantum accelerators add 8 co-processors to the Quantum Computer multiblock.\n\nIt's important to note that all crafting patterns being run by the quantum computer are able to share all co-processors, so it's probably a good idea to invest in a great amount of these.
If you built a larger multiblock than you have resources to fill all the empty slots, these blocks can be used on the inside for no additional benefit.

By combining some coal and iron, I can create a new alloy.

I always thought coal burned at a low temperature — turns out I was wrong.

With this machine, I can now produce steel — one step closer to finding my way back home.
I can use this compressor to turn ingots into plates.
The Quantum armor from the Advanced AE can also be used instead of the space suit.\n\n&lNOTE:&r The space suit chest plate &nis still required!&r
pf.quest.chapter.back_to_reality.back_to: Now with this item in hand I'm finally able to open a portal back home.

I've finally managed to craft a teleporter that should take me back home.

I've spent so much time on this planet and I'm worried what awaits me back home.

Was everything fine after the accident or not?

I guess all my questions will be answered once I go through it.{@pagebreak}&6&lNotes:&r&r

- Right click the portal with this item in your main or off hand.

- This will consume the final star so either bring more with you, or a waystone so you can go back.

When I first stepped through the teleporter, the sun was hitting my eyes and it took me a second to adjust my vision.

It seemed like I was finally back in my old world, but then the vision started to clear up.

After looking around, I knew that this isn't my world.

For one, my world wasn't floating in the sky with nothing else around me but the island I stood on.

Have I reached somewhere new?

Will I have to start all over again in these new lands?

I can only imagine what awaits me...

A big thank you from me, for playing this pack and reaching this point.

It was a journey to develop it and I'm sure it was a journey for you to play it.

Even though this pack ends here, it doesn't mean the story is over.

New stories and adventures await us all.

Wish you all the best and happy crafting,

GacBL :)
